summary: Configured sudo command logging on node1: sudo now logs via syslog facility local2 (via /etc/sudoers.d/syslog-local2), and rsyslog (/etc/rsyslog.d/sudo-commands.conf) routes local2.* to /var/log/sudo-commands.log then discards it (~), keeping entries out of /var/log/messages. Verified logging works and stays isolated from the general log both before and after a full node restart (boot_id changed from 16724682... to 8a973a0c...), confirming persistence.
actions_performed: Inspected OS (RHEL 7.9), rsyslog/sudo packages, and existing rsyslog.conf rules
Created /etc/sudoers.d/syslog-local2 with 'Defaults syslog=local2' and validated with visudo -cf
Created /etc/rsyslog.d/sudo-commands.conf routing local2.* to /var/log/sudo-commands.log and discarding further processing (~) so entries don't reach /var/log/messages
Restarted rsyslog and verified active status

Ran test sudo commands and confirmed they appear in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with timestamp, user, and command, and confirmed grep for COMMAND= in /var/log/messages showed no new entries post-config
Captured baseline boot_id and healthy service state
Issued 'shutdown -r now' in background, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec became available again
Confirmed boot_id changed (16724682-15d4-4e48-bfb9-a2913f22f416 -> 8a973a0c-8c80-4de9-8dee-057f318601fd), proving actual restart
Post-restart verified rsyslog active, sudo commands still logging correctly to dedicated file, and still excluded from /var/log/messages

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands are recorded with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Log file shows entries like 'Aug 26 10:39:46 node1 sudo: antrieb : TTY=unknown ; PWD=... ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/whoami' confirming timestamp, user, and command are captured

evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log (/var/log/messages)
evidence.summary: grep for COMMAND= in /var/log/messages shows only pre-config-change entries; commands issued after rsyslog restart (whoami, id, cat) do not appear there
Captured boot_id 16724682-15d4-4e48-bfb9-a2913f22f416, confirmed rsyslog active, and sudo-commands.log had 14 healthy entries prior to restart

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable mid-reboot (connection timeout), then came back with a new boot_id 8a973a0c-8c80-4de9-8dee-057f318601fd, differing from the baseline 16724682-...

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo logging and exclusion from general log
evidence.summary: After restart, rsyslog is active, new sudo command (whoami) logged with timestamp/user to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and /var/log/messages still shows no new COMMAND= entries, confirming the config persisted across reboot
